_doc: A9 mechanical fixes (lead 20 Nov): " (recommended)" added to unmarked verify sentences of should-points

fixes.before: Verify that the manufacturer ensures that the following data is retained for a minimum of 30 years after the expiry date of the product, unless a longer period is provided for in the marketing authorisation: identification (including batch number) of critical raw materials and other substances that come into contact with the cells or tissues used as starting materials that may have a significant impact on the safety of the finished ATMP (e.g. reagents of biological origin, scaffolds, matrixes); and, where applicable, identification (including batch number) of all other active substances that are contained in the ATMPs. Verify also that, for biological materials, the identification of the supplier, species and anatomical environment from which the materials originate is described (recommended).
fixes.after: Verify that the manufacturer ensures that the following data is retained for a minimum of 30 years after the expiry date of the product, unless a longer period is provided for in the marketing authorisation: identification (including batch number) of critical raw materials and other substances that come into contact with the cells or tissues used as starting materials that may have a significant impact on the safety of the finished ATMP (e.g. reagents of biological origin, scaffolds, matrixes); and, where applicable, identification (including batch number) of all other active substances that are contained in the ATMPs (recommended). Verify also that, for biological materials, the identification of the supplier, species and anatomical environment from which the materials originate is described (recommended).

fixes.before: Verify that, if a quality defect is discovered or suspected in a batch, consideration is given to checking other batches and in some cases other products, in order to determine whether they are also affected. Verify that, in particular, other batches which may contain portions of the defective batch or defective components are investigated (recommended).
fixes.after: Verify that, if a quality defect is discovered or suspected in a batch, consideration is given to checking other batches and in some cases other products, in order to determine whether they are also affected (recommended). Verify that, in particular, other batches which may contain portions of the defective batch or defective components are investigated (recommended).

fixes.before: Verify that the decisions made during and following quality defect investigations reflect the level of risk presented by the quality defect as well as the seriousness of any non-compliance with respect to the requirements of the marketing authorisation/product specification file or GMP. Verify that such decisions are timely to ensure that patient and animal safety is maintained, in a way that is commensurate with the level of risk presented by those issues (recommended).
fixes.after: Verify that the decisions made during and following quality defect investigations reflect the level of risk presented by the quality defect as well as the seriousness of any non-compliance with respect to the requirements of the marketing authorisation/product specification file or GMP (recommended). Verify that such decisions are timely to ensure that patient and animal safety is maintained, in a way that is commensurate with the level of risk presented by those issues (recommended).

fixes.before: Verify that appropriate CAPAs are identified and taken in response to a quality defect. Verify that the effectiveness of such actions is monitored and assessed (recommended).
fixes.after: Verify that appropriate CAPAs are identified and taken in response to a quality defect (recommended). Verify that the effectiveness of such actions is monitored and assessed (recommended).

fixes.before: Verify that, after a product has been placed on the market, any retrieval of it from the distribution network as a result of a quality defect is regarded and managed as a recall. This does not apply to the retrieval (or return) of samples of the product from the distribution network to facilitate an investigation into a quality defect issue/report (recommended).
fixes.after: Verify that, after a product has been placed on the market, any retrieval of it from the distribution network as a result of a quality defect is regarded and managed as a recall (recommended). This does not apply to the retrieval (or return) of samples of the product from the distribution network to facilitate an investigation into a quality defect issue/report (recommended).

fixes.before: Verify that the sponsor has implemented a procedure for the rapid unblinding of blinded products, where this is necessary for a prompt recall. Verify that the sponsor ensures that the procedure discloses the identity of the blinded product only in so far as is necessary (recommended).
fixes.after: Verify that the sponsor has implemented a procedure for the rapid unblinding of blinded products, where this is necessary for a prompt recall (recommended). Verify that the sponsor ensures that the procedure discloses the identity of the blinded product only in so far as is necessary (recommended).

fixes.before: Verify that, in case of outsourced activities, a contract describes the role and responsibilities of the manufacturer, the marketing authorisation holder and/or sponsor and any other relevant third parties in relation to assessment, decision-making, and dissemination of information and implementation of risk-reducing actions relating to a defective product. Verify that such contracts also address how to contact those responsible at each party for the management of quality defect and recall issues (recommended).
fixes.after: Verify that, in case of outsourced activities, a contract describes the role and responsibilities of the manufacturer, the marketing authorisation holder and/or sponsor and any other relevant third parties in relation to assessment, decision-making, and dissemination of information and implementation of risk-reducing actions relating to a defective product (recommended). Verify that such contracts also address how to contact those responsible at each party for the management of quality defect and recall issues (recommended).

fixes.before: Verify that the nature and extent of controls applied to utility systems are commensurate with the risk to product quality associated with the utility. Verify that the impact is determined via a risk assessment and documented as part of the CCS (recommended).
fixes.after: Verify that the nature and extent of controls applied to utility systems are commensurate with the risk to product quality associated with the utility (recommended). Verify that the impact is determined via a risk assessment and documented as part of the CCS (recommended).

fixes.before: Verify that water flow remains turbulent through the pipes in water distribution systems to minimize the risk of microbial adhesion, and subsequent biofilm formation. Verify that the flow rate is established during qualification and is routinely monitored (recommended).
fixes.after: Verify that water flow remains turbulent through the pipes in water distribution systems to minimize the risk of microbial adhesion, and subsequent biofilm formation (recommended). Verify that the flow rate is established during qualification and is routinely monitored (recommended).

fixes.before: Verify that it is ensured that the shipping of the IMPs minimises any risk of exposure to conditions that could impact quality and integrity of the product. Verify that this includes security of the product (e.g. against adulteration, tampering or theft), ensuring that the applicable principles of the guidelines on Good Distribution Practice (GDP) of medicinal products for human use are taken into consideration, including but not limited to, documentation, transportation (including selection of container and packaging, qualification and/or validation activities, monitoring of transport conditions) and outsourced activities (recommended).
fixes.after: Verify that it is ensured that the shipping of the IMPs minimises any risk of exposure to conditions that could impact quality and integrity of the product (recommended). Verify that this includes security of the product (e.g. against adulteration, tampering or theft), ensuring that the applicable principles of the guidelines on Good Distribution Practice (GDP) of medicinal products for human use are taken into consideration, including but not limited to, documentation, transportation (including selection of container and packaging, qualification and/or validation activities, monitoring of transport conditions) and outsourced activities (recommended).

fixes.before: Verify that if it becomes necessary to change the expiry date, an additional label is affixed to the investigational ATMP, and that this additional label states the new expiry date and repeats the batch number. It may be superimposed on the old expiry date but, for quality control reasons, not on the original batch number (recommended).
fixes.after: Verify that if it becomes necessary to change the expiry date, an additional label is affixed to the investigational ATMP, and that this additional label states the new expiry date and repeats the batch number (recommended). It may be superimposed on the old expiry date but, for quality control reasons, not on the original batch number (recommended).

fixes.before: Verify that if it becomes necessary to change the expiry date, an additional label is affixed to the investigational medicinal product, and that this additional label states the new expiry date and repeats the batch number and clinical trial reference number. It may be superimposed on the old expiry date but, for quality control reasons, not on the original batch number (recommended).
fixes.after: Verify that if it becomes necessary to change the expiry date, an additional label is affixed to the investigational medicinal product, and that this additional label states the new expiry date and repeats the batch number and clinical trial reference number (recommended). It may be superimposed on the old expiry date but, for quality control reasons, not on the original batch number (recommended).

fixes.before: Verify that, for grade A areas, particle monitoring is undertaken for the full duration of critical processing, including equipment assembly, except where duly justified (e.g. contaminants in the process that would damage the particle counter or when this would present a hazard, e.g. live pathogenic organisms). Verify that in such cases monitoring takes place during equipment set-up operations (i.e. prior to exposure of the product to the hazard) (recommended).
fixes.after: Verify that, for grade A areas, particle monitoring is undertaken for the full duration of critical processing, including equipment assembly, except where duly justified (e.g. contaminants in the process that would damage the particle counter or when this would present a hazard, e.g. live pathogenic organisms) (recommended). Verify that in such cases monitoring takes place during equipment set-up operations (i.e. prior to exposure of the product to the hazard) (recommended).

fixes.before: Verify that, while at rest, the HVAC system is not interrupted, as this may trigger the need for re-qualification. Verify that, in the event of an interruption, a risk assessment is conducted to determine any actions that may be needed taking account of the activities performed in the affected areas (e.g. additional monitoring) (recommended).
fixes.after: Verify that, while at rest, the HVAC system is not interrupted, as this may trigger the need for re-qualification (recommended). Verify that, in the event of an interruption, a risk assessment is conducted to determine any actions that may be needed taking account of the activities performed in the affected areas (e.g. additional monitoring) (recommended).

fixes.before: Verify that points to consider in such a risk assessment include but are not limited to: iii. In depth process knowledge such as: the specific product type, including particle burden and whether there exists any risk of impact on filter integrity values, such as the potential to alter integrity-testing values and therefore prevent the detection of a non-integral filter during a post-use filter integrity test; pre-filtration and processing steps, prior to the final sterilising grade filter, which would remove particle burden and clarify the product prior to the sterile filtration (recommended).
fixes.after: Verify that points to consider in such a risk assessment include but are not limited to: iii (recommended). In depth process knowledge such as: the specific product type, including particle burden and whether there exists any risk of impact on filter integrity values, such as the potential to alter integrity-testing values and therefore prevent the detection of a non-integral filter during a post-use filter integrity test; pre-filtration and processing steps, prior to the final sterilising grade filter, which would remove particle burden and clarify the product prior to the sterile filtration (recommended).
